I've witnessed numerous instances where either the cursor bugbot or Claude has found a bug and recommended a reasonable fix. The fix has been implemented and then the LLM has argued the case against the fix and requested the code be reverted... I turned off the auto code reviews and stuck them in request only mode.

Do you have actual experience with bugbot? Its live in our org and is actually pretty good, almost none of its comments are frivolous or wrong, and it finds genuine bugs most reviewers miss... Bugbot is now a valuable part of our SD process.
I assume that this is the same as when Cursor spontaneously decides to show code review comments in the IDE as part of some upsell? In that case yes I'm familiar and they were all subtly wrong.
I've found Bugbot to be shockingly effective at finding bugs in my PRs. Even when it's wrong, it's usually worth adding a comment, since it's the kind of mistake a human reviewer would make.
